newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine proposes '97 budget deficit at 5.5 pct GDP.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine proposes '97 budget deficit at 5.5 pct GDP.

text.p: Ukraine's revised 1997 draft budget calls for a deficit of 5.8 billion hryvnia, or 5.5 percent of gross domestic product (four percent by Western calculations), the deputy finance minister said on Friday.

Stanyslav Bukovynsky told a news conference the deficit would be covered by 2.4 billion hryvnia in foreign credits, 1.7 billion hryvnia from Treasury-bill revenues and 1.7 billion hryvnia from the National Bank of Ukraine.
The draft, which calls for tough spending cuts, proposes revenues of 37 billion hryvnia and expenditures of 42.8 billion hryvnia.

Bukovynsky said deficit financing would come from sources such as the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF), which agreed last week to allow Ukraine to raise the deficit by a percentage point.

He said the central bank's contribution would be covered partly by an expected 400 million hryvnia loan from the IMF. Ukraine has also said it plans to issue foreign bonds next year but has not given a target figure.
"These sources will cover the deficit, if parliament agrees to this," Bukovynsky said. "We want to keep the deficit at 5.5 percent of GDP."

The constitution states the annual budget must be passed by January 1, but the largely left-leaning parliament is expected to reject many of the budget proposals, which also call for cuts in benefits to Chernobyl victims and other social programmes.
The draft, which aims to increase industrial production next year, includes proposals for wide-reaching tax reforms to broaden the tax base and relieve the tax burden on businesses.

Ukraine reached agreement with the IMF last week to raise the deficit from an originally proposed three percent of GDP, which paves the way for Ukraine to receive a $2.5-3.0 billion three-year Extended Fund Facility (EFF) from the IMF. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
